To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) water conservation behaviours and water use are not necessarily correlated; (ii) the prestige of sustainable living is not necessarily a motivator of water conservation behaviours; (iii) water conservation behaviour does not necessarily lead to water conservation; and (iv) water conservation behaviours may lead to water conservation in the long run.

high per capita water users are those who live in large households with a high number of adults; those who live in a house with a large garden, who water their gardens often, who water more often than is allowed under the restrictions and who do not water their garden efficiently.
the prestige of sustainable living is a significant determinant of water use and that the prestige of sustainability is a significant predictor of water use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the nature of the relationship between the prestige of sustainability and water conservation behaviour.
understanding the relationship between water conservation behaviour and the level of water use in the household, and the extent of congruity between stated water use and actual metered consumption.

the relationship between householders’ perceptions and their behaviour, the relationship between household water use and the characteristics of the householders, and the implications of this for water demand management.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

high water users are not a homogeneous group and that the water use behaviour of high consumers is not necessarily a result of a lack of knowledge about water restrictions and water saving techniques, nor is it a function of a lack of concern for the environment.
the prestige of water conservation is not enough to change the behaviour of the highest water users.
water conservation behaviours are more important in predicting water consumption than socio-economic characteristics of the household.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
water users who are high consumers of water are more likely to be older, live in larger households, have a higher annual household income, and are less likely to be in the workforce.
